name: Behavior Variance
summary: Adds small, human-like variation to Smart Action waits and aim actions. On by default for every binding.

where.text: Edit your Config (pencil icon). Under Mappings, press the "..." and select Behavior Simulation to set the variance values. To turn variance off for a single binding, edit your Config and press the watch icon. It turns red when off.

citations.quote: To edit the current Config, press the pencil icon.
To configure variance, under Mappings press the "..." and select Behavior Simulation.
To disable variance per-binding, edit your Config and press the watch icon.
The icon will turn red when it's off.

definition.text: Behavior variance simulates natural human behavior patterns for specific Smart Actions.

citations.quote: Behavior variance is used to add simulate natural human behavior patterns for specific smart actions.

plainWords.text: Wait Variance is a percentage above or below each Wait. XIM's example: 20% on a 150 ms wait gives a wait between 120 ms and 180 ms.

citations.quote: Wait Variance is a percentage of variance above or below the specified value.
For example, 20% for a 150ms wait time means, when run, the wait will be between 120ms and 180ms.

plainWords.text: Aim Magnitude Variance is a percentage above or below the action's speed. Aim Angle Variance is an offset above or below the action's angle.

citations.quote: Aim Magnitude Variance is a percentage of variance above or below the specified value.
The Aim Angle Variance value is a variance offset above or below the specified value.

plainWords.text: It affects Smart Actions (waits, and Aim Magnitude and Aim Angle actions), not your own mouse aim.

citations.quote: Behavior variance is used to add simulate natural human behavior patterns for specific smart actions.
Or, a recoil control sequence's Aim Magnitude and Angle actions will be slightly offset from the values you specified:

plainWords.reasoning: The guide defines it for "specific smart actions" and its settings are Wait, Aim Magnitude and Aim Angle variance. None of them names mouse, thumbstick or gyro aim.

guidance.text: It is on by default and set per binding. Press the watch icon while editing a binding to turn it off; the icon turns red.

citations.quote: Variance is controlled per-binding and is enabled by default.
To disable variance per-binding, edit your Config and press the watch icon.
The icon will turn red when it's off.

guidance.text: By default, Wait Variance is 20%, so each Wait can run anywhere from 20% shorter to 20% longer than the value you set (XIM's example: a 150 ms Wait runs between 120 ms and 180 ms). Aim Angle Variance defaults to 2.5° and Aim Magnitude Variance to 2.5.

citations.quote: By default, this value is 20%.
For example, 20% for a 150ms wait time means, when run, the wait will be between 120ms and 180ms.
By default, these values are 2.5°/s and 2.5° respectively.
Aim Magnitude Variance is a percentage of variance above or below the specified value.
For example, 2.5% for a 10°/s magnitude action means, when run, the value will be between 10.25°/s and 9.75°/s.

guidance.caveat: XIM's two pages disagree on the unit for Aim Magnitude Variance. The Simulate Analog Behavior page gives its default as 2.5°/s. The Behavior Variance page calls it a percentage, and its example uses 2.5% on a 10°/s action (10.25°/s to 9.75°/s).

guidance.text: Setting a variance value to 0 turns that type of variance off for all bindings.

citations.quote: For all variance settings, setting to 0 will disable it for all bindings.

guidance.text: Turning off Wait Variance makes timing perfect, but less human.

citations.quote: While disabling wait variance will make your sequence timing perfect, it also means it will behave less human.

guidance.text: Turning off variance on a binding also turns off Simulate Analog Behavior for that binding.

citations.quote: When disabling Variance for a binding, this will also disable Simulate Analog Behavior for that binding as well.

guidance.text: Only if you use SAB: keep Wait Variance and Aim Variance on, and don't disable variance on bindings.

citations.quote: Wait Variance in on
Aim Variance is on
Do not disable variance on bindings

guidance.caveat: Applies only when Simulate Analog Behavior (SAB) is on. SAB is a controller-output feature for games with extra input requirements.

confusions.name: Simulate Analog Behavior
confusions.note: In the same Behavior Simulation menu, but shapes the stick and trigger output instead of Smart Action values.

confusions.name: Magnitude and Angle Quantization
confusions.note: "Magnitude" and "Angle" here mean Smart Action values. Quantization snaps your own aim.
